persistedBacklogEvidence.shape: source lag increased progressively, then queued messages caught up to sub-second latency

conclusion: Real temporary service consumption backlog, not a 60-second clock offset or persistent provider delay. Six subscriptions do not exhaust the configured budget. Serialized per-message database work and expensive status scans share the sole database connection; the status query alone consumed about 768ms in a same-data benchmark.
minimalFix: Migration 0021 adds quote-only covering indexes for the two MAX timestamp queries. No source timestamp rewriting, dropping queued trades, unsafe SQLite durability change, or host adapter modification.
remaining: Indexes address the proven hot read path; they do not prove bounded latency under arbitrary subscription count or exchange bursts. Per-trade multi-statement writes and one socket per symbol/timeframe remain throughput limits. Receive timestamps are currently processing/persistence times, so an explicit socket-read timestamp would improve future attribution.
